body.p: Used to query or configure client parameters.
HTTPS one-way authentication: The terminal verifies the server. Only the server certificate needs to be configured.
HTTPS two-way authentication: Server cert, client cert, and client private key required (not supported yet).
Due to limited terminal computing power and storage, two-way authentication may be time-consuming. One-way authentication is recommended for general needs.
<id>: Client instance created by the AT+HTTPCREATE command.
8: Configure print mode: 1 indicates that the received string is printed in hexadecimal format; 0 indicates string mode (default is 0).
<value>: The value set according to the different type.

<encode>: Indicates whether to use hexadecimal format when inputting certificate data. The input can be sent either in hexadecimal or as a plain string. It is recommended to use the default value 1, which indicates that hexadecimal format is used for serial port input.

1. As the server certificate, client certificate, and client private key have two storage methods, they are handled in the following two cases respectively (HARDCODE_USER_CERT_PK is set to 1 by default).

ul.li: When HARDCODE_USER_CERT_PK = 0, after HTTP request is successfully sent, server cert, client cert, and client private key configured via AT+HTTPCFG are automatically cleared to free memory and prevent high memory usage. However, they are still consumed during handshake. Reconfiguration is required before re-sending HTTP request.

When HARDCODE_USER_CERT_PK = 1, certificates stored in flash (last three 4 KB sectors of FOTA area, max 4 KB each). This avoids high memory usage during handshake. However, FOTA area reuse may cause certificate erasure. Reconfigure before each use is recommended.

body.p: 2. For one-way authentication, only the server certificate needs to be configured.
3. Client private key and certificate can be generated as follows (using OpenSSL as an example):
openssl req -new -key ./private.pem -out csr.pem ＃Generate CSR using private key file.
openssl x509 -req -days 365 -in csr.pem -signkey ./private.pem -out ./file.crt ＃Generate certificate file using private key and CSR.

4. When using string input for certificate and private key, do not change certificate format; otherwise, mbedTLS parsing fails. Since some serial tools do not support special chars like \r\n, hex input via serial port is recommended.
